newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end floor trade above 2,900-points.
newsitem.headline: German shares end floor trade above 2,900-points.

text.p: German shares end bourse trade above the psychologically-important 2,900-point threshold, lifted by a late rally on Wall Street overnight, the ever-strengthening dollar and a firm German debt market.

The DAX index of 30 blue-chip German shares closed at 2,906.34 points, up 20.21 points or 0.70 percent, a convincing breach of the 2,900-point marker deemed important by analysts for buoying market sentiment.
"The steady dollar and a higher Wall Street are helping us today," said one dealer. The dollar traded strongly firmer at 1.5725 marks by the end of bourse trade.

Traders said that they were holding back from pushing the DAX towards any really significant gains as they waited to see U.S. rate implications of U.S. producer price and payroll data, due Thursday and Friday respectively.
The markets would also be closely monitoring German GDP and jobless data, due on Thursday morning, dealers said.
Banking shares were the most actively traded, benefiting from perennial takeover rumours in the sector and the apparent slow-down in the rally that chemical stocks saw in 1996.
Commerzbank in particular was strong, ending up 1.53 pfennigs at 42.68 marks, and the second highest-traded stock of the morning.

"The chemicals rally is over. Now the banks can finally take over the pole position," said one trader. Deutsche Bank, Germany's largest commercial bank, gained 1.90 marks to 73.95 and was the third highest-traded stock in bourse trade.
Utility RWE AG ended 1.55 marks higher at 66.50 after the German stock exchange said it was suspending trade in its majority-held Rheinelektra AG and Lahmeyer units pending an announcement.
The two companies earlier last year said they were considering a merger.
